assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Continents or Small Continents, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Tokugawa has one persona and that is the one planned here; he is Japan's Leader Pass leader, not Hojo Tokimune, so Divine Wind's half-price districts do not apply. The plan counts only Bakuhan's domestic route bonus and its penalty on international routes; read the full Bakuhan text on the leader screen at turn 1 and treat any further clause as a bonus.

verdict.one_line: Settle eight to ten cities in a tight coastal cluster, give each a Commercial Hub or Harbor so it adds a Trader, send the routes into a capital stacked with every district type, never trade abroad, and decide by turn 70 what the Culture, Science and Gold are for.
verdict.why: Bakuhan pays Culture, Science and Gold on domestic routes for every specialty district at the destination, so the empire's income is the number of routes times the districts in the city they end in. Meiji Restoration makes that district stack the best-adjacency layout as well, and the Electronics Factory covers a tight cluster with Production and later Culture. None of this points at a victory by itself, and the price is the whole international trade game, which costs a Science victory nothing: a Spaceport needs no foreign route, no alliance and no Tourism. Culture is the second direction because the same yields buy civics just as well, but Bakuhan's penalty takes the Tourism a foreign route would carry, so that direction needs the map to hand over the Culture pieces first.

must_have: Room for seven or eight cities within about ten tiles of the capital, since every city is a Trader and every route must be short and inside your own borders.
A coastal capital, or coast one move from the start; Harbors are half the cluster's Trade Route capacity and the capital wants both a Harbor and a Commercial Hub.
prefer: Flat or gently hilled land around the capital, so a ring of seven or eight districts can touch the City Center and each other.
A river beside the capital for the Hanging Gardens and Commercial Hub adjacency.
The Great Barrier Reef in reach, so one Campus adds Reef adjacency to the district adjacency Meiji Restoration already gives.
The nearest rival on another continent or across a wide sea; isolation is cheap when nobody is close.
map_check.no_go: A start boxed in by two rivals with room for three or four cities. Bakuhan multiplies routes by districts, and four cities is four routes into a hub that never fills; nothing in the kit buys land.
map_check.fallback: Settle what there is as tightly as possible and run the boxed-in trigger: four Samurai with a Battering Ram take the nearest rival's two closest cities once Military Tactics lands, then make peace. If the neighbours are too strong for that, play the four cities for Science with every route into the capital and accept a slower game.

kit_levers.name: Bakuhan
kit_levers.buys: Domestic Trade Routes gain +1 Culture, +1 Science and +1 Gold for every specialty district at the destination; international routes, city-state routes included, lose yields and the Tourism they would carry.
kit_levers.exploit: The yield is routes times districts at the destination, so the plan makes the capital the destination for one route from every city and stacks every district type in it, including an Encampment and a Holy Site that would be wasted elsewhere; further Traders go to a second hub. Eight routes into a seven-district capital is fifty-six Culture, fifty-six Science and fifty-six Gold a turn before the second hub adds its share, and none of it needs a foreign city.

kit_levers.name: Meiji Restoration
kit_levers.buys: Every district gets a full +1 adjacency from each adjacent district instead of the half point other civilizations get.
kit_levers.exploit: The capital's districts go in a ring touching the City Center and each other, so the stack Bakuhan wants is also the best-adjacency layout. In the small cities the second district touches the Commercial Hub or Harbor already there; it is never walked off to a distant Mountain.

kit_levers.name: Samurai
kit_levers.buys: A Medieval melee unit that fights at full Combat Strength however badly damaged it is.
kit_levers.exploit: The isolation's army. Two to four Samurai on the coastal approaches hold the Trader roads and the capital against a landing without Walls in every city. On a boxed-in start the same four take a neighbour's two nearest cities before Medieval Walls and then go home.

kit_levers.name: Electronics Factory
kit_levers.buys: A Factory whose Production reaches every city within six tiles and which adds Culture to each of them once Electricity is researched.
kit_levers.exploit: A tight cluster puts every city inside one Electronics Factory's reach. Build it in the central Industrial Zone, research Electricity as soon as it is in reach, and the Culture it adds pays for the late civics on either direction.

kit_levers.name: Sakoku
kit_levers.buys: AI Tokugawa likes civilizations that avoid conquest and dislikes any leader who has captured a capital.
kit_levers.exploit: Only matters when an AI plays Tokugawa. For your own play it is a reminder that the boxed-in war takes border cities, never a capital, so the peaceful neighbours this plan wants as friends and allies stay friendly.

options.when_it_fits: The default. Take it when at turn 70 the cluster holds six or more cities, the capital can grow to nineteen population for a seventh district, and the World Rankings show no met civilization more than a few techs ahead. Isolation costs a Science victory nothing: Campuses ringed by districts, Universities bought with Bakuhan Gold, Rationalism and the Spaceport need no foreign route, alliance or Tourism.

Take it only when the map has already handed over the pieces by turn 70: two Cultural city-states met, a Classical wonder in the capital, Breathtaking coast for Seaside Resorts, and no Culture-specialist rival among the met civilizations. Theater Squares ringed by districts and Electronics Factory Culture make the civic side easy, but Bakuhan's penalty removes trade-route Tourism, so the Tourism must come from Open Borders, Great Works, National Parks and Seaside Resorts.

direction.commit_test: At turn 100 check three things. The second district in every city outside the capital is the direction's (Campus for Science, Theater Square for Culture); the Economic and Wildcard slots hold the direction's cards (Natural Philosophy, later Rationalism, or Literary Tradition); and the Bakuhan Gold of the last twenty turns bought the direction's buildings (Libraries and Universities, or Amphitheaters). A mix of districts and a growing treasury means the bonus is being banked and the plan has failed its own test.

phases.name: Seat the cluster
phases.objective: Settle a coastal capital, found three more cities four tiles apart so every future route is short and inside your borders, take City Patron Goddess, place the capital's Campus, and finish Foreign Trade so the first Trader runs a domestic route into the capital by turn 40, while the Scout starts the information plan by meeting every civilization and city-state in reach.

checkpoints.test: Four cities, the first Trader on a domestic route into the capital, and the capital Campus built or under way?

Found City Patron Goddess, or God of the Sea if the capital has four or more sea resources.
First Trader from the second city to the capital; never to a foreign city and never to a city-state.

phases.name: Every city a Trader
phases.objective: Grow the cluster to eight cities, give every one a Commercial Hub or Harbor so each adds a point of Trade Route capacity, run every route into the capital, adopt Classical Republic, write the direction down by turn 70, and have a Delegation with every civilization met so the isolation does not leave you blind.

First district in every inland city and the second in the capital: a point of Trade Route capacity, and City Patron Goddess adds 25% Production toward it wherever it is the first district.
First district in every coastal city instead of the Commercial Hub: the same capacity plus Fishing Boat Food. The capital gets both because both count at the destination.
One per point of capacity, built in a city other than the capital and sent to the capital.
Second city's Campus for Recorded History; the capital's is already up.
Construction Eureka in a river city and Production for its first district.
On the coastal city that faces the sea lanes; a plundered Trader costs more than the Walls, and they give the Engineering Eureka.
Fishing Boats and Farms; the capital must reach ten population for Civil Service and nineteen for its seventh district.

checkpoints.test: Era checkpoint: is the bonus being spent? Five or more specialty districts in the capital, every route domestic and ending in a hub, the last three civics on the direction's path, and no city missing the direction's building while the treasury holds more than 500 Gold?

decision_triggers.name: A foreign route looks bigger
decision_triggers.if: A foreign city or a city-state such as Kumasi shows a larger number in a Trader's destination list than the capital, usually because the capital has fewer than four specialty districts.
decision_triggers.then: Send the Trader to the capital anyway and move the capital's next district to the top of its queue. Bakuhan's penalty applies to every international route, city-states included, and a route abroad gives up the per-district bonus for good; the fix is the destination's districts, never the border.

decision_triggers.name: Boxed in
decision_triggers.if: At turn 70 the cluster has fewer than six city sites and a neighbour's cities sit within eight tiles of the capital.
decision_triggers.then: Keep the direction, but once Military Tactics lands take the neighbour's two nearest cities with four Samurai and a Battering Ram before it has Medieval Walls. Each becomes a trade origin and a set of districts; make peace the turn the second one falls and never take its capital.

decision_triggers.name: Rival out of reach
decision_triggers.if: At an era checkpoint the Listening Post, the Embassies or the World Rankings show a rival a full era ahead on the direction's race.
decision_triggers.then: Pivot: from Science to Culture, Theater Squares become every city's next district and the Electronics Factory Culture goes to the Tourism civics; from Culture to Science, Campuses do. The flat curve makes the switch affordable; drifting between the two does not.

decision_triggers.name: Trader in danger
decision_triggers.if: A barbarian camp appears within five tiles of a route, a Trader is plundered, or a rival fleet is sighted off the cluster's coast.
decision_triggers.then: Clear the camp or put two Samurai on the road before re-sending, and build Walls in the coastal city that is threatened. A route lost mid-way costs every turn it had left, not one turn.

decision_triggers.name: Hub full
decision_triggers.if: The capital has as many specialty districts as its population allows and a district is waiting.
decision_triggers.then: Point the next Traders at the second hub, put Liang's Zoning Commissioner there, and grow the capital with a Neighborhood and Surplus Logistics before the next district.

abort.trigger: Turn 150 with no direction committed: second districts split between Campuses and Theater Squares, more than 1,000 Gold of Bakuhan income unspent, and the civic queue picked in tree order.
actions: Pick the direction the cluster is already closest to; with a ringed Campus in the capital and isolation costing it nothing, that is almost always Science. Commit fully; Linear leaders lose by drifting, not by collapsing.
Spend the banked Gold today on the direction's buildings in every city that lacks them.
Re-pick the civic queue toward The Enlightenment and Class Struggle for Science, or Humanism and Opera and Ballet for Culture.

fail_state: Turn 220 with ten tidy Japanese cities, a capital ringed with districts, every route domestic and the treasury full, and nothing pointing anywhere: Campuses in some cities and Theater Squares in others, no Spaceport site, no Tourism lead, and no idea how far ahead the rival on the other continent is because nobody sent a Delegation or a Spy. Bakuhan has paid for two hundred turns and bought a comfortable Score game.
common_mistakes: Sending one Trader abroad because its number looks bigger. Bakuhan's penalty applies to every international and city-state route; a small domestic number means the capital needs districts, not that the route should leave.
Spreading districts to chase terrain adjacency. Meiji Restoration pays for touching districts; a Campus walked three tiles to a Mountain loses its neighbours and gains nothing.
Building Encampments and Holy Sites in every city. They pay through Bakuhan only at the destination; outside the capital they are dead Production.
Re-sending a finished Trader on its old route out of habit. Each time a route ends, send it to whichever hub has the most specialty districts now.
Skipping the information plan. Isolation hides rival progress; Delegations, Embassies, the Caravel lap and a Spy are the only way to know the direction is still reachable.
Settling a scattered empire. A city ten tiles from the capital is a long, plunderable route outside the Electronics Factory's reach; the cluster stays tight.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset with the Leader Pass (Japan, Tokugawa, Bakuhan, Meiji Restoration, Samurai, Electronics Factory).

The civ-info text puts Amenities for cities near the capital and District Tourism after Flight under Meiji Restoration. In Gathering Storm, Meiji Restoration is the district-to-district adjacency rule only; if those clauses exist they belong to Tokugawa's own ability text, so the plan treats them as a bonus and depends on neither. The civ-info source label says New Frontier Pass; Tokugawa came with the Leader Pass.

The civ-info text gives no numbers for Bakuhan; the plan uses +1 Culture, +1 Science and +1 Gold per specialty district at the destination, and treats the international penalty as large enough that no foreign route is worth sending. The Electronics Factory's Culture to cities within six tiles requires Electricity.
